rulings.challenge_claim: The row's declared divine-title signal is asserted with two byte-tier labels but no quoted Hebrew form anywhere in the row, and its closing-title framing omits the same title's third site in the chapter while the span's own bytes do name Israel.
rulings.grounds: All three arms are real, but the tier arm needs correcting and the naming arm is narrower than stated. Arm one, upheld and sharpened: the row asserts that the title closes this span as it also closes the previous one, 'a recurring closing-title texture', with a 'tier: byte' label hung on each ref and NO Hebrew form and NO object named anywhere in the row. Re-derived, the tier depends entirely on which object is meant, which is exactly what the row fails to say -- the ATTESTED TOKENS are differently prefixed and do not recur, בִּקְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Isa.41.16) returning tier NONE against וּקְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Isa.41.20); but the un-prefixed TITLE CORE does recur at BYTE tier inside both, as the bare form standing later in this same stretch shows, קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Isa.43.3) re-collating at byte tier against oshb:Isa.41.16 and against oshb:Isa.41.20. So the corrected finding is not that the label is false but that it is unverifiable as written: with no form and no named object, the row's own recurrence claim cannot be checked, and under the semantic-class discipline the object must be named before the tier. Arm two, upheld: the title stands at 3 verses in this chapter (sweep: 3 verses, contiguous qadosh skeleton, ch 41 -- oshb:Isa.41.14, 41.16, 41.20), so קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Isa.41.14, byte tier against its own verse) is a third, non-closing site one span back that the closing-title framing does not disclose. Arm three, refined DOWN: 'without renaming Israel explicitly' does sit against אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Isa.41.17, byte tier) and the name stands in the span's first and last verses, but in both places it stands inside a DIVINE TITLE and never as the addressee, and the row's own rejected alternative already states the point precisely as 'without renaming the addressee'. That arm is a prose-precision defect in one field, not a substantive error. Seam uncontested: both PE marks verify under the claimed type (oshb:Isa.41.16, oshb:Isa.41.20, tier-3, single-witness) and no paseq and no ketiv/qere note falls inside oshb:Isa.41.17-Isa.41.20. Severity low stands.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: name the swept object BEFORE the tier and quote the forms -- the attested tokens בִּקְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Isa.41.16) and וּקְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Isa.41.20) are differently prefixed and return tier NONE against each other, while the un-prefixed title core re-collates at byte tier inside both; write whichever object the row actually means and label only that. device_notes: disclose the third, non-closing site קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Isa.41.14) with the chapter digit (sweep: 3 verses, contiguous qadosh skeleton, ch 41), so the closing-title framing is not built on a partial list. boundary_rationale: change 'without renaming Israel explicitly' to the precise form the rejected alternative already uses -- the ADDRESSEE is not renamed -- and note that the name stands at אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Isa.41.17, byte tier) and again in the closing title, in two divine titles rather than as the addressee. This same object-before-tier correction reads back onto the qadosh-title labels in the fear-not row one span earlier, so treat it as a sweep across the title citations in this stretch, not a spot fix. TEST the cure must pass: for every title citation the named object must re-collate to the tier written -- the attested-token pairing must return NONE and only the un-prefixed core may be called byte -- which is the check the original label could not survive because no object was named at all; and the chapter digit must name its swept object and unit.

rulings.challenge_claim: Disclosure-object coverage is complete and byte-correct, but two byte-true devices straddle the row's own close seam undisclosed and the cross-span summons echo is asserted with no Hebrew form.
rulings.grounds: Credit first, re-derived: every disclosure object inside oshb:Isa.41.21-Isa.41.29 verifies and is disclosed under its claimed type -- PE at oshb:Isa.41.20 and oshb:Isa.41.29, paseq at oshb:Isa.41.22 tallied with no intra-verse position asserted, ketiv/qere at oshb:Isa.41.23 disclosed without adjudicating the reading -- which is the fullest symmetry in this cluster. The defects hold. The close seam at web:Isa.41.29|web:Isa.42.1 is straddled twice and disclosed neither time: the presentative particle opening הֵ֣ן כֻּלָּ֔ם אָ֥וֶן (oshb:Isa.41.29, byte tier against its own verse) is answered immediately by הֵ֤ן עַבְדִּי֙ (oshb:Isa.42.1, byte tier against its own verse), the two particles re-collating against each other at accent_stripped tier, and the verse-initial digit verifies exactly -- that particle opens 18 verses book-wide (sweep: 18 verses, verse-initial hen, skeleton tier), four of them clustered at oshb:Isa.41.11, 41.24, 41.29 and 42.1. The second device is the spirit-noun reversal, ר֥וּחַ וָתֹ֖הוּ (oshb:Isa.41.29, byte tier) against רוּחִי֙ עָלָ֔יו (oshb:Isa.42.1, byte tier), the two nouns re-collating at skeleton tier through the suffixed form. Together they argue that the servant presentation answers the idol verdict across the cut, which neither the PE mark nor the speaker change disposes of on its own, so the disclosure is owed. The third arm holds too: the web:Isa.41.1 echo is asserted with no quoted form although the bytes state it plainly -- קָרְב֥וּ רִֽיבְכֶ֖ם and הַגִּ֨ישׁוּ֙ עֲצֻמ֣וֹתֵיכֶ֔ם (oshb:Isa.41.21, byte tier each against its own verse) against יַחְדָּ֖ו לַמִּשְׁפָּ֥ט נִקְרָֽבָה (oshb:Isa.41.1, byte tier) -- so the rival architecture the row discloses rests on English idiom rather than on the shared roots that carry it. Severity low is correct: the cut itself is not overturned.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: disclose both close-seam devices with pointed splices and collate-true tiers -- הֵ֣ן כֻּלָּ֔ם אָ֥וֶן (oshb:Isa.41.29) against הֵ֤ן עַבְדִּי֙ (oshb:Isa.42.1), the particles at accent_stripped tier, with the verse-initial digit (sweep: 18 verses, verse-initial hen, skeleton tier; four at oshb:Isa.41.11, 41.24, 41.29, 42.1), and ר֥וּחַ וָתֹ֖הוּ (oshb:Isa.41.29) against רוּחִי֙ עָלָ֔יו (oshb:Isa.42.1) at skeleton tier -- and state why the speaker change plus the mark still carry the cut. device_notes: splice and tier the web:Isa.41.1 summons echo instead of carrying it in English -- קָרְב֥וּ רִֽיבְכֶ֖ם and הַגִּ֨ישׁוּ֙ עֲצֻמ֣וֹתֵיכֶ֔ם (oshb:Isa.41.21) against יַחְדָּ֖ו לַמִּשְׁפָּ֥ט נִקְרָֽבָה (oshb:Isa.41.1), byte tier each against its own verse. boundary_rationale: strike the tier-4 chapter-division descriptor ('bringing the chapter to its own end'), which is never boundary evidence, leaving the PE mark as single-witness corroboration. TEST the cure must pass: a cross-seam re-check at web:Isa.41.29|web:Isa.42.1 must return no straddling device left undisclosed -- the check the original failed -- every added run must re-collate to exactly the tier written, and no chapter-division wording may remain in the boundary prose.

rulings.challenge_claim: The four-verse bound rests on an envelope that the bytes make a thread, and on a frame onset labelled 'tier: byte' with no frame form quoted -- the byte arm of a frame-based seam claim is missing.
rulings.grounds: Both arms verify, and the first is sharper than stated. The justice-noun stands in 3 of the span's 4 verses (sweep: 3 verses, the mishpat noun in ch 42 -- oshb:Isa.42.1, 42.3, 42.4, skeleton tier): מִשְׁפָּ֖ט לַגּוֹיִ֥ם יוֹצִֽיא (oshb:Isa.42.1), לֶאֱמֶ֖ת יוֹצִ֥יא מִשְׁפָּֽט (oshb:Isa.42.3) and יָשִׂ֥ים בָּאָ֖רֶץ מִשְׁפָּ֑ט (oshb:Isa.42.4), byte tier each against its own verse. So the term is a sustained thread, not an envelope. Re-derived further, the bracket the row claims is the WEAKEST of the three pairings available: the full opening run returns tier NONE against both oshb:Isa.42.3 and oshb:Isa.42.4, while the repeated verb יוֹצִֽיא (oshb:Isa.42.1) re-collates against oshb:Isa.42.3 at skeleton tier and the closing verse uses a different verb entirely -- so the tightest byte link inside the span is opening-to-MEDIAL, which is the opposite of an inclusio. Arm two verifies: the seam claim labels the closing frame 'tier: byte' with nothing quoted, while the form is כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר הָאֵ֣ל יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.42.5, byte tier), a divine frame carrying the ha-El title, and the frame's owner class is what a koh-amar claim must name -- the royal-messenger uses of this formula sit only in the narrative zone, not here (sweep: 2 verses, the koh-amar formula within Isa 41:17-43:7 -- oshb:Isa.42.5 and oshb:Isa.43.1, both divine-owned, skeleton tier). Cross-seam, two devices go unremarked, and their tiers must be named honestly: the earth-noun link בָּאָ֖רֶץ (oshb:Isa.42.4) into רֹקַ֥ע הָאָ֖רֶץ (oshb:Isa.42.5) returns tier NONE between the attested tokens, sharing only the noun stem under different prefixes, and the presentative particle הֵ֤ן עַבְדִּי֙ (oshb:Isa.42.1) answering oshb:Isa.41.29 crosses the onset seam at accent_stripped tier. The bound itself is NOT overturned: it rests on the tier-1 frame onset at oshb:Isa.42.5 plus the PE marks at oshb:Isa.41.29 and oshb:Isa.42.4, both verifying under the claimed type, and low confidence is correctly held. Nothing in this ruling decides the servant referent, which the row correctly leaves open. Severity medium.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: withdraw the envelope framing and write what the bytes carry -- the justice-noun is a sustained thread through 3 of the 4 verses (sweep: 3 verses, the mishpat noun in ch 42), with the repeated verb יוֹצִֽיא (oshb:Isa.42.1) linking to oshb:Isa.42.3 at skeleton tier and the closing verse using a different verb -- and let the bound rest on the tier-1 frame onset, which already carries it. strongest_rejected_alternative or boundary_rationale: quote the frame and name whose it is -- כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר הָאֵ֣ל יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.42.5, byte tier), a divine frame carrying the ha-El title (sweep: 2 verses, the koh-amar formula within Isa 41:17-43:7, both divine-owned) -- instead of the bare 'tier: byte' label with no form. device_notes: disclose the two seam-straddling devices at their true tiers, the presentative particle הֵ֤ן עַבְדִּי֙ (oshb:Isa.42.1) against oshb:Isa.41.29 at accent_stripped tier, and the earth-noun stem shared with רֹקַ֥ע הָאָ֖רֶץ (oshb:Isa.42.5) at stem level only, the attested tokens returning tier NONE. No respan. TEST the cure must pass: the revised bound must still stand with the envelope sentence DELETED outright -- only the ground that survives that deletion may be written, which is the check that killed the original -- every koh-amar citation must name its frame owner and quote the form, and every added run must re-collate to the tier named, with 'byte' reserved for runs that return byte.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row locates a count-only paseq inside a named clause, leaves a byte-true answer pair straddling its close seam undisclosed, and labels an unquoted cross-span echo 'tier: byte' on uneven byte support.
rulings.grounds: Credit first: the frame is quoted in full and its owner correctly named -- כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר הָאֵ֣ל יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.42.5, byte tier) is a divine frame carrying the ha-El title -- and the PE marks at oshb:Isa.42.4 and oshb:Isa.42.9 verify under the claimed type. All three defects hold. (1) The paseq at oshb:Isa.42.5 is real in the single-witness inventory, but the row places it 'inside the divine-frame clause opening this span'. That layer is COUNT-ONLY and intra-verse position is unsourceable; naming the clause IS a position claim, and the row's own trailing disclaimer of a position claim does not cure the clause it has just located it in. (2) The close seam carries an undisclosed answer pair, and its tier must be named honestly: וַֽחֲדָשׁוֹת֙ אֲנִ֣י מַגִּ֔יד (oshb:Isa.42.9, byte tier against its own verse) is picked up one verse later by שִׁ֣יר חָדָ֔שׁ תְּהִלָּת֖וֹ (oshb:Isa.42.10, byte tier against its own verse), the new-things and new-song forms sharing the root at stem level and returning tier NONE as attested tokens; and the praise-noun the span withholds from idols at וּתְהִלָּתִ֖י (oshb:Isa.42.8, byte tier) is what the following verses render, at תְּהִלָּת֖וֹ (oshb:Isa.42.10) and וּתְהִלָּת֖וֹ בָּאִיִּ֥ים יַגִּֽידוּ (oshb:Isa.42.12), the pair oshb:Isa.42.10 against oshb:Isa.42.12 re-collating at skeleton tier (sweep: 3 verses, the tehillah noun in ch 42 -- oshb:Isa.42.8, 42.10, 42.12; 2 verses, the kavod noun -- oshb:Isa.42.8, 42.12, skeleton tier). A skeleton-tier cohesion thread across the row's own seam is admissible evidence WITH the tier named, so the disclosure is owed. (3) The backward echo is labelled 'tier: byte' at two refs with no form quoted, and the support is uneven in exactly the way OL states -- and worse: הָרִֽאשֹׁנ֖וֹת (oshb:Isa.42.9) re-collates against oshb:Isa.41.22 only at SKELETON tier, the shared former-things noun standing there as הָרִאשֹׁנ֣וֹת (oshb:Isa.41.22, byte tier against its own verse), while against oshb:Isa.41.26 it returns tier NONE, that verse carrying only מֵרֹאשׁ֙ (oshb:Isa.41.26, byte tier), a from-the-beginning adverbial and a different object. So one tier label covers two unlike objects and is wrong for BOTH. Severity medium.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: remove the clause-location for the paseq at oshb:Isa.42.5 -- tally it as count-only and single-witness with no clause, phrase, or position named, since the disclaimer cannot cure a location already written. device_notes: disclose the close-seam thread with its true tiers -- וַֽחֲדָשׁוֹת֙ אֲנִ֣י מַגִּ֔יד (oshb:Isa.42.9) into שִׁ֣יר חָדָ֔שׁ תְּהִלָּת֖וֹ (oshb:Isa.42.10) at stem level, the attested tokens returning tier NONE, and the praise-noun from וּתְהִלָּתִ֖י (oshb:Isa.42.8) into תְּהִלָּת֖וֹ and וּתְהִלָּת֖וֹ בָּאִיִּ֥ים יַגִּֽידוּ, the later pair at skeleton tier (sweep: 3 verses, the tehillah noun in ch 42; 2 verses, the kavod noun) -- and state why the PE mark plus the form shift still carry the cut. device_notes: split the one joint 'tier: byte' echo label into two named objects at their true tiers -- the former-things noun הָרִֽאשֹׁנ֖וֹת (oshb:Isa.42.9) against הָרִאשֹׁנ֣וֹת (oshb:Isa.41.22) at skeleton tier, and oshb:Isa.41.26, whose מֵרֹאשׁ֙ is a different object, either dropped from the echo or cited separately as a root-level parallel, never under one byte label. TEST the cure must pass: every recurrence label must equal the tier returned for the exact run quoted with the object named first, so neither echo ref may carry 'byte' -- the check that killed the original -- and a paseq-position re-check must find no intra-verse location asserted anywhere in the row.

rulings.challenge_claim: Every cited mark and the onset form verify, but a high-confidence cut leaves a byte-true catchword pair straddling its onset seam undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: The defect is real and the severity is right, but the framing must be corrected on the word that carries it: the straddling devices are NOT byte-true recurrences. Verified credit: the onset splice re-collates at byte tier, PE at oshb:Isa.42.9 and SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.42.13 both verify under the claimed type with PE never conflated with SAMEKH, and no paseq and no ketiv/qere note falls inside oshb:Isa.42.10-Isa.42.13, so in-span disclosure is complete. Verified gap: the row's device_notes carries NO cross-seam content at all while declaring high confidence, and three threads run across its onset seam -- שִׁ֣יר חָדָ֔שׁ תְּהִלָּת֖וֹ (oshb:Isa.42.10) takes up וַֽחֲדָשׁוֹת֙ אֲנִ֣י מַגִּ֔יד (oshb:Isa.42.9) one verse back; the praise-noun runs from וּתְהִלָּתִ֖י (oshb:Isa.42.8) into תְּהִלָּת֖וֹ and וּתְהִלָּת֖וֹ בָּאִיִּ֥ים יַגִּֽידוּ (sweep: 3 verses, the tehillah noun in ch 42); and the glory-noun runs from וּכְבוֹדִי֙ (oshb:Isa.42.8) into כָּב֑וֹד (oshb:Isa.42.12) (sweep: 2 verses, the kavod noun). Corrected finding: each phrase is byte tier against ITS OWN verse, which is what the packet's labels actually say, but as RECURRENCES across the seam these are stem-level threads -- the new-things/new-song pair returns tier NONE as attested tokens and the praise-noun pair oshb:Isa.42.10 against oshb:Isa.42.12 reaches skeleton tier. That still triggers the disclosure obligation, since a skeleton-tier cohesion driver is admissible WITH its tier named, but it is materially weaker than 'byte-true', and writing the cure at byte tier would reproduce the exact tier-label defect this cluster is otherwise being corrected for. The cut is not overturned: the form shift from first-person divine speech to plural imperative is byte-plain and the marks corroborate; what is carrying an undisclosed rival is the high confidence band. Severity low.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: add the cross-seam disclosure this row currently lacks entirely, at the TRUE tiers -- שִׁ֣יר חָדָ֔שׁ תְּהִלָּת֖וֹ (oshb:Isa.42.10) taking up וַֽחֲדָשׁוֹת֙ אֲנִ֣י מַגִּ֔יד (oshb:Isa.42.9) at stem level with the attested tokens at tier NONE, the praise-noun from וּתְהִלָּתִ֖י (oshb:Isa.42.8) into תְּהִלָּת֖וֹ and וּתְהִלָּת֖וֹ בָּאִיִּ֥ים יַגִּֽידוּ with the later pair at skeleton tier, and the glory-noun וּכְבוֹדִי֙ (oshb:Isa.42.8) into כָּב֑וֹד (oshb:Isa.42.12) (sweep: 3 verses, the tehillah noun in ch 42; 2 verses, the kavod noun). confidence: re-weigh the high band against that disclosed rival and lower it if the rival survives, since the band, not the cut, is what the gap was propping up; if it is retained, say in one sentence why the imperative shift plus the mark outrank the thread. NOTE for the author wave, applying to this row and to its two neighbours in this stretch: write these threads as skeleton or stem-level, never as byte -- a cure written at byte tier fails the same check that condemned the tier labels elsewhere in this cluster. TEST the cure must pass: every added run must re-collate to exactly the tier written, with 'byte' used only for a run that returns byte against the ref it is cited at, and a cross-seam re-check at web:Isa.42.9|web:Isa.42.10 must return no thread left undisclosed.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row's unnamed-referent prose is silent about its own span naming Jacob and Israel, and both of its seams carry byte-true devices it does not disclose.
rulings.grounds: All three arms verify. Credit first, re-derived: the disclosure objects are complete and correct -- SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.42.17, PE at oshb:Isa.42.25, and both ketiv/qere notes at oshb:Isa.42.20 and oshb:Isa.42.24 verify under the claimed type -- and the internal hearing-root chain genuinely supports holding the eight verses as one unit against the web:Isa.42.21 cut the row tests (sweep: 4 verses, the shama root in ch 42 -- oshb:Isa.42.18, 42.20, 42.23, 42.24, skeleton tier), opening at הַחֵרְשִׁ֖ים שְׁמָ֑עוּ (oshb:Isa.42.18, byte tier). Arm one: the span's own bytes name the plundered party at יַעֲקֹ֛ב וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל לְבֹזְזִ֖ים (oshb:Isa.42.24, byte tier) -- the strongest in-span datum bearing on the held question -- and the row is silent about it even while citing that very verse for its ketiv/qere note. The defect is the SILENCE, not the referent prose, which is accurate on its own terms: the names at oshb:Isa.42.24 belong to the plundered party, not to the servant designation, and whether they are the same party is precisely the held classic. This ruling does not decide it and the cure must not either. Arm two: the blindness lexeme reaches into this span's opening from וְהוֹלַכְתִּ֣י עִוְרִ֗ים (oshb:Isa.42.16, byte tier), re-collating against oshb:Isa.42.18 at accent_stripped tier through וְהַעִוְרִ֖ים, and continuing at עִוֵּר֙ (oshb:Isa.42.19, byte tier) (sweep: 5 verses, the blind lexeme in chs 42-43 -- oshb:Isa.42.7, 42.16, 42.18, 42.19, 43.8). Mitigation, recorded but not a downgrade: the neighbouring row on the other side of that seam does disclose this device, so the seam-pair is covered from one side -- a seam-pair cure is one edit, and this row still owes its half. Arm three, unmitigated and the heaviest: the close seam is a CROSS-PART seam, and it carries וַתִּבְעַר בּ֖וֹ (oshb:Isa.42.25, byte tier) answered by וְלֶהָבָ֖ה לֹ֥א תִבְעַר בָּֽךְ (oshb:Isa.43.2, byte tier), stem-shared with the attested tokens at tier NONE, while the two names recur at בֹּרַאֲךָ֣ יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְיֹצֶרְךָ֖ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Isa.43.1, byte tier), likewise stem-level against oshb:Isa.42.24. NEW FINDING, neither lens: the boundary prose carries barred register -- 'marking the chapter's end and this part's own closing verse' is a tier-4 chapter-division descriptor plus explicit part-order talk, and the same part-positional habit recurs at 'in an earlier span of this part' in the two neighbouring rows of this cluster. Severity medium.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: disclose the in-span name-pair יַעֲקֹ֛ב וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל לְבֹזְזִ֖ים (oshb:Isa.42.24, byte tier) NEUTRALLY -- as the party named plundered in this span's own bytes, expressly held open against the servant designation of web:Isa.42.19 and not resolved in either direction -- since the held classic forbids deciding it and the disclosure obligation does not touch the referent. device_notes: disclose both seams at their true tiers -- the blindness lexeme וְהוֹלַכְתִּ֣י עִוְרִ֗ים (oshb:Isa.42.16) against וְהַעִוְרִ֖ים (oshb:Isa.42.18) at accent_stripped tier, continuing at עִוֵּר֙ (sweep: 5 verses, the blind lexeme in chs 42-43); and across the close seam וַתִּבְעַר בּ֖וֹ (oshb:Isa.42.25) against וְלֶהָבָ֖ה לֹ֥א תִבְעַר בָּֽךְ (oshb:Isa.43.2) at stem level with the attested tokens at tier NONE, plus the name recurrence at בֹּרַאֲךָ֣ יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְיֹצֶרְךָ֖ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Isa.43.1), also stem-level. Because that close seam is a cross-part seam, the disclosure must be written on BOTH sides as one edit. boundary_rationale: strike the tier-4 chapter-division descriptor and the part-order phrase 'this part's own closing verse'; cross-row references stay verse-anchored only. rulings.challenge_claim: The onset argument rests on an adversative and a divine frame the row never quotes, its close seam is argued against a byte-mislabelled rival, and the seam it cuts carries an undisclosed answer pair.
rulings.grounds: Every arm verifies. Arm one: the row argues 'the adversative onset' and a divine address while splicing only the participial epithets that follow it -- the frame itself is וְעַתָּ֞ה כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Isa.43.1, byte tier), one of only two divine-speech frames in this cluster's whole span (sweep: 2 verses, the koh-amar formula within Isa 41:17-43:7 -- oshb:Isa.42.5 and oshb:Isa.43.1, both divine-owned, neither royal-messenger, skeleton tier), and the row splices בֹּרַאֲךָ֣ יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְיֹצֶרְךָ֖ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Isa.43.1, byte tier) instead. A frame-based seam claim owes the frame form and its owner class. Arm two, confirmed exactly: the row places the gathered-nations address at web:Isa.43.8, but oshb:Isa.43.8 reads הוֹצִ֥יא עַם עִוֵּ֖ר (byte tier), a summons of the BLIND PEOPLE that ties back across the previous seam -- עִוֵּר֙ (oshb:Isa.42.19, byte tier) re-collates against oshb:Isa.43.8 at accent_stripped tier -- while the gathered nations open one verse later at כָּֽל הַגּוֹיִ֞ם נִקְבְּצ֣וּ יַחְדָּ֗ו (oshb:Isa.43.9, byte tier). The rival is therefore refused against a mislocated description. Arm three: the onset seam, which is a CROSS-PART seam, carries וַתִּבְעַר בּ֖וֹ (oshb:Isa.42.25, byte tier) answered by וְלֶהָבָ֖ה לֹ֥א תִבְעַר בָּֽךְ (oshb:Isa.43.2, byte tier), stem-shared with the attested tokens at tier NONE, and the name pair of oshb:Isa.42.24 recurring at בֹּרַאֲךָ֣ יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְיֹצֶרְךָ֖ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Isa.43.1) at stem level -- undisclosed. Arm four: the sole parashah citation is keyed with a web: prefix on an MT-keyed single-witness layer; the coordinate is identity-numbered so the arithmetic holds, but unlike the other rows in this stretch there is no correctly keyed entry standing beside it, so the row cites that layer only on the wrong witness. NEW FINDING, neither lens, and the most consequential thing here: the strongest_rejected_alternative NAMES the rival and never rejects it -- it states the extension through the witness summons and stops, supplying no ground at all, while every neighbouring row in this cluster supplies one and this row carries HIGH confidence. A rival that is described but not refused leaves that confidence band unwarranted on the row's own face. Second new finding: the span carries a divine-title site at קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Isa.43.3, byte tier), whose title core re-collates at BYTE tier against oshb:Isa.41.16 and oshb:Isa.41.20 where the same title closes two units in this stretch, and the row discloses nothing about it and carries no title key in its signal list. Severity medium.
rulings.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative: supply the missing refusal ground -- as written the field names the extension through web:Isa.43.8-Isa.43.9 and never rejects it -- and argue the refusal from the bytes at the corrected location, namely that the address changes at web:Isa.43.9 with כָּֽל הַגּוֹיִ֞ם נִקְבְּצ֣וּ יַחְדָּ֗ו (oshb:Isa.43.9, byte tier) while web:Isa.43.8 is a summons of the blind people, הוֹצִ֥יא עַם עִוֵּ֖ר (oshb:Isa.43.8, byte tier), reaching back to oshb:Isa.42.19 at accent_stripped tier. boundary_rationale: correct the rival's location from web:Isa.43.8 to web:Isa.43.9, and quote the onset frame with its owner named -- וְעַתָּ֞ה כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Isa.43.1, byte tier), a divine frame (sweep: 2 verses, the koh-amar formula within Isa 41:17-43:7, both divine-owned) -- rather than arguing the adversative and the frame in English while splicing only the epithets. device_notes: disclose the cross-part onset seam at its true tiers -- וַתִּבְעַר בּ֖וֹ (oshb:Isa.42.25) against וְלֶהָבָ֖ה לֹ֥א תִבְעַר בָּֽךְ (oshb:Isa.43.2) at stem level, attested tokens at tier NONE, and the name recurrence at בֹּרַאֲךָ֣ יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְיֹצֶרְךָ֖ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל -- written as ONE edit with the row on the other side of that seam. device_notes and observed_substrate_signals: disclose the in-span title site קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Isa.43.3), whose core is byte-identical to the title closing the units at oshb:Isa.41.16 and oshb:Isa.41.20, and say what distinguishes it -- it stands inside an appositional divine self-identification with a further clause following, not in the verse's closing clause as at those two sites -- and add the divine_title.* key. boundary_evidence_refs: re-key 'web:Isa.42.25 (petuchah, single-witness)' to an oshb: coordinate; that layer is MT-keyed and this row has no correctly keyed entry beside it. confidence: re-weigh the high band once the rival is actually refused and the seam devices are disclosed. TEST the cure must pass: the rejected_alternative must contain a refusal ground that survives with the parashah citation deleted from the sentence; the rival's verse location must re-check against the bytes at web:Isa.43.9, not web:Isa.43.8 -- the check the original failed; every added run must re-collate to the tier written; and no parashah annotation may remain on a WEB key.
